providers.title: One-sided inverses
providers.scope: If ab = 1 and a has a left inverse, then ba = 1. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finite groups
providers.scope: K[G] is stably finite for every finite group G and every field K. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finite supports
providers.scope: A pair with ab = 1 and ba != 1 lives on the finitely generated subgroup generated by the supports. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Range projections
providers.scope: The range projection of an idempotent in matrices over the group von Neumann algebra has the same trace. Uses the trace of the Kervaire course.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finitely generated fields of characteristic zero
providers.scope: Every finitely generated field of characteristic zero embeds in the complex numbers. Uses the fundamental theorem of algebra (core course).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Kaplansky's theorem in characteristic zero
providers.scope: K[G] is stably finite for every group G and every field K of characteristic zero. Uses the trace of the Kervaire course.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Kaplansky's direct-finiteness conjecture fails (OpenAI)
providers.scope: There are a finite field K of characteristic two, a finitely presented group G with odd torsion and a, b in K[G] with ab = 1 and ba != 1; proved in the last lesson. Uses (LIN) and (PLANE).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A finitely presented group that is neither sofic nor surjunctive (OpenAI)
providers.scope: The group of Theorem 5.1 is not sofic, and b defines an injective cellular automaton that is not surjective. Uses Theorem 5.1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Group-algebra elements as automata
providers.scope: c -> T_c is an injective algebra homomorphism into the linear maps of K^G, with T_c T_d = T_cd for right neighbours. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The transfer to automata
providers.scope: If ab = 1 over a finite field, T_b is injective with image the fixed points of T_ba, and it misses delta_h whenever (ba - 1)_h != 0. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A finite obstruction to surjectivity
providers.scope: A nonsurjective automaton over a countable group misses a finite pattern. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Uniform local injectivity
providers.scope: An injective automaton over a countable group determines x(1) from the image on a fixed finite set. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Sofic groups are surjunctive (Gromov, Weiss)
providers.scope: Every injective cellular automaton over a sofic group with a finite alphabet is surjective. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Counterexamples over finite fields live on nonsofic groups
providers.scope: If ab = 1 != ba in K[G] with K finite, then G is neither surjunctive nor sofic. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The incidence criterion (OpenAI)
providers.scope: A regular incidence system of girth at least 12 with vectors satisfying the pairing identities and m < t <= m l^2 gives a finitely presented group and a, b with ab = 1 != ba; proved in lesson 5. Uses (PLANE).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The glued group is finitely presented
providers.scope: The relators of length at most three define the glued group. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The local groups embed (OpenAI)
providers.scope: If the incidence graph has girth at least 12, every copy of F_l^2 embeds in the glued group. Uses (PLANE).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Local groups as unions of lines
providers.scope: The sum over K_v is 1 plus the sums of sigma_f - 1 over the lines through v. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The rectangular identity
providers.scope: UP = U, PT = T and UT = I_m. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The twisted extension contains H
providers.scope: H = N x <z> embeds in the twisted extension L, proved with a permutation representation. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Orthogonal character idempotents
providers.scope: Q_alpha Q_beta = delta Q_alpha for linear forms on K_*. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Twisted averages
providers.scope: tau_v e P_v tau_v^-1 = e Q_(alpha_v). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Packing
providers.scope: J_0 C = eP. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A square one-sided inverse
providers.scope: a_mat b_mat = I_m. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The reverse defect
providers.scope: b_mat a_mat - I_m != 0, certified by the specialization -kappa X^T X - I_t. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Matrix units of a finite group algebra
providers.scope: The p_ij in K[(Z/l)^m x| S_m] are linearly independent matrix units. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Two elements with ab = 1 != ba
providers.scope: The scalar outputs a and b in K[L x F]. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finite presentation
providers.scope: G = L x F is finitely presented and contains an element of order l. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Interpolation on an index simplex
providers.scope: Evaluation on S_d is an isomorphism from polynomials of total degree at most d. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Line sums
providers.scope: A polynomial of total degree at most q - 2 sums to zero over every affine line of Q^n. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The pairing supplied by holes (OpenAI)
providers.scope: Interpolation polynomials of the holes give vectors with the pairing identities and m < t <= m l^2. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A regular line system with holes and girth 12 (OpenAI)
providers.scope: For large h there are holes and a D-regular family of affine lines avoiding them with incidence girth at least 12; proved in the last lesson. Uses (LIN).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Direction spaces
providers.scope: Planes W_r and spaces E_j any ten of which form a direct sum. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The local trade
providers.scope: Replacing the fan of a hole in a plane by parallel lines removes the hole and keeps every other degree. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Compatible holes
providers.scope: Holes with the size bounds, one per plane, bounded occupancy and no exceptional rectangle with four witnesses. Uses (LIN) for the bound on s.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Replacement lines
providers.scope: Replacement lines avoid the holes, are disjoint within a label and form no exceptional rectangle. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A vector in a random plane
providers.scope: A fixed nonzero vector lies in a uniform random plane of E_j with probability (q^2 - 1)/(q^(b-1) - 1). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Short polygons
providers.scope: Candidate polygons are rectangles or pentagons of three kinds, and their events have probability p_*^(2g). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Event bounds
providers.scope: The event probabilities at each slab variable add up to O(q^-7). No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The local lemma (special case)
providers.scope: Events determined by at most four independent variables, with sums at most 1/16 at each variable, can be avoided together. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Slab partitions
providers.scope: A three-dimensional slab has a line partition with a given axis whose other lines are transverse to the axis direction. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The trades
providers.scope: After all trades every point off the holes has degree D, and lines of one label are disjoint. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
